code: The fuzzer input is appended to a newly created IPv6 message and sent with otIp6Send().
note: Attacker-controlled bytes become the outbound CoAP/IPv6 payload that drives the vulnerable parser.

code: Incoming CoAP request is parsed, URI path options are concatenated, and the matching resource handler is dispatched.
note: The crafted request reaches the MeshCoP active-set handler through the CoAP request dispatcher.

code: Active dataset SET requests are forwarded to DatasetManager::HandleSet().
note: This is the entry point for processing the attacker-controlled MeshCoP dataset TLVs.

code: Tlv::GetTlv(aMessage, Tlv::kMeshLocalPrefix, sizeof(meshLocalPrefix), meshLocalPrefix) copies the Mesh Local Prefix TLV into a fixed-size stack object and then compares its length bytes with the local prefix using memcmp().
note: The bug is that memcmp() uses meshLocalPrefix.GetLength() bytes without bounding it to the 8-byte destination/source object size, so an oversized TLV length causes an out-of-bounds read.
